title: Good news for the night shift

card.keepWhy: Good news goes to the outsiders first.
sources: Luke 2:8-20 (shepherds in the same country, watching and keeping the night watches over their flock; an angel of the Lord, the brightness of God shone round about them, and they feared with a great fear; “Fear not; for, behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy, that shall be to all the people: For, this day, is born to you a Saviour, who is Christ the Lord … you shall find the infant wrapped in swaddling clothes, and laid in a manger”; a multitude of the heavenly army praising God: “Glory to God in the highest; and on earth peace to men of good will”; they came with haste and found Mary and Joseph, and the infant lying in the manger; they made known what had been told them, and all that heard wondered; “But Mary kept all these words, pondering them in her heart”). Douay-Rheims.
1 Samuel 16:11 and 17:15 (David a shepherd of Bethlehem).
Roman Missal, the Gloria (“Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace to people of good will”), sung or said on Sundays outside Advent and Lent (General Instruction of the Roman Missal 53).
check: Luke 2:17-18 says the shepherds made known what they had been told and all who heard wondered; the caption says “they told everyone”. Confirm.
The lesson says “most Sundays” for the Gloria (it is omitted in Advent and Lent). Confirm.

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? have you ever worked a night shift, or been up at 3 a.m. while everyone else slept?
options: then this story is for you. the news came to the night shift.
oh, that counts double. watch this.
then picture the ones who are. they’re in this story.

steps.line: That same night, in the fields outside Bethlehem, shepherds were keeping watch over their flock. The night shift, while the town slept.

steps.q: Suddenly an angel stands before the terrified shepherds. What does the angel say first?
steps.why: Do not be afraid, the words Zechariah and Mary heard from an angel too. Then: good news of great joy, for all the people.

steps.line: Suddenly an angel stood before them, and the glory of the Lord shone all around. They were terrified.
“Do not be afraid. I bring you good news of great joy for all the people. Today a Savior is born. You’ll find a baby lying in a manger.”

steps.q: The sign of a Savior is a baby in a feeding trough. Why give shepherds that sign?
o: It was the only baby in Bethlehem that night
A trough was their world, not a palace’s
A manger was a sign of a royal birth
steps.why: Not a crown, a feeding trough: something from their own working world. The news came in their language.

steps.line: Then the sky filled with angels, singing: “Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace to people of good will.”

steps.q: The angels’ song opens the Gloria at Mass. In which season do Catholics stop singing it on Sundays?
steps.why: In Advent (and Lent) the Gloria goes quiet, so that at Christmas the angels’ song comes back, loud, on the night it was first sung.

steps.line: The shepherds hurried into Bethlehem and found Mary and Joseph, and the baby lying in the manger, just as they’d been told.
They told everyone what they’d heard, and people were amazed. But Mary kept all these things, pondering them in her heart.

steps.q: Why would Luke’s first readers smile at shepherds near Bethlehem being the first to hear?
o: King David was a Bethlehem shepherd boy
steps.why: Bethlehem was David’s town, and David was out with the sheep when he was called to be king. (Bethlehem actually means “house of bread.”)

say: here’s what i love. big news usually goes to palaces first. luke sends it to a field, to the night shift, to men who smelled like sheep.
catholics see a pattern here: God’s good news goes to the outsiders first, and the outsiders become the messengers. king david was a shepherd boy from bethlehem too.

steps.q: Everyone else is amazed and talking. Why might Luke end the scene with Mary quiet, pondering?
o: She doubted what the shepherds said
She was holding it close to understand it
She was too worn out to say anything
steps.why: The shepherds spread it; Mary keeps it. Both are ways of saying yes. Some good news takes a lifetime to understand.

today.say: this week, notice someone on the night shift of life: the cleaner, the nurse, the cashier at the late-night store. say thank you, or bring them something warm. if you pray, you can say the angels’ line for them: glory to God, and peace.
options: lovely. good news for the night shift.
then this one’s for you. the angels came to your shift first.
